correctness.rationale: For all finite connected undirected positive-weight graphs, p>0, positive convictions and stubbornness, the coercive potential has a positive minimizer (nonzero constant perturbation; connectedness excludes boundary zeros). At a positive equilibrium the max-coordinate ratio rules out two solutions. Writing H=κL+diag[σ_i((p+1)x_i^p-u_i)], the exact equilibrium identity gives Hx=pσ_i x_i^(p+1)>0. diag(x)Hdiag(x) has nonpositive off-diagonals and positive row sums pσ_i x_i^(p+2), proving H positive definite. Implicit differentiation yields D′=−(Lx)^T H^{-1}(Lx), strictly negative unless all u_i equal; at κ=0 H_0=diag(pσ_i u_i) gives the claimed right slope. Boundedness of x between min and max convictions and κLx=f(x) imply x→c1 with c=(Σσu/Σσ)^(1/p), and the EXACT identity D=(2κ²)^−1 f(x)^T L†f(x) yields the stated strictly positive resistance coefficient and exact inverse-square decay for nonconstant u. The one-sided κ=0 and constant-u cases were checked; no inference from finite tests substitutes for this derivation.
